claims.claim: Hong Kong can tighten rent control on subdivided units.
Rent control should be done in a measured way.
A hard cap on initial rents should be avoided.
The case for acting starts with the tenants.
Mr Chan pays 5,800 dollars for a 120 sq ft cubicle.
Mr Chan's rent is about a third of his household income.
SDU tenants pay a premium of 15 to 25 percent per square foot compared with mainstream flats.
Landlords warn that members will leave the market if returns fall below mortgage cost.
The stock numbers do not show landlords leaving so far.
The estimated stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025.
The stock grew even after the 2021 tenancy control.
The strongest objection is that the 2021 control was mild, so that growth says little about a hard cap.
The working paper argues that hard caps on levels show consistent contraction effects.
The working paper argues that the 2021 ordinance caps increases and so shows small or null effects.
The author would tighten gradually and watch the stock figures before going further.

cites.sentence: Mr Chan pays 5,800 dollars for a 120 sq ft cubicle, about a third of his household income [D3p1].
Across the market, SDU tenants pay a premium of 15 to 25 percent per square foot compared with mainstream flats [D1p1].
The landlords warn that members will leave the market if returns fall below mortgage cost [D5p2].
The stock numbers do not show that so far: the estimated stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025, including after the 2021 tenancy control [D2p1].
The working paper argues exactly this: hard caps on levels show consistent contraction effects, while the 2021 ordinance caps increases and so shows small or null effects [D6p2].
